maria_onboard: heads up 1 — multiple users confused by our JS quickstart using `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'`. Errors vary: `Cannot use import statement outside a module` and `client.generate is not a function` depending on CJS/ESM mismatch. Can we pin a short guide in onboarding?

sam_sdk: yep. Short checklist: prefer ESM `import` (edge, modern Next). For CommonJS consumers show the require compat: `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference').default || require('@redwood/inference')`. Call that a compatibility workaround, not preferred.

kev_tests: add TS notes: recommend `esModuleInterop: true` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true` in tsconfig for CJS targets, or set `module: 'ESNext'` for ESM builds. Also show `import type` for type-only imports to avoid runtime pulls in ESM builds.

emma_devex: also document package.json fields: "type": "module" makes .js files ESM. If users have an `exports` map, include both `import` and `require` entries so require() still resolves. Small snippet in docs: "exports":{ ".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}}.

sam_sdk: troubleshooting tips: (1) check if bundler rewrote exports (use `node -p "require.resolve('@redwood/inference')"`), (2) try the `.default` guard if require returns an object, (3) for Jest with ts-jest use `extensionsToTreatAsEsm` + `useESM:true` or run jest with `--experimental-vm-modules` on older Node versions.

kev_tests: for CI add a tiny matrix test (Node ESM, Node CJS, Next Edge build) and assert `typeof client.generate === 'function'` after import. That catches default vs named mismatches early.

emma_devex: I'll draft a PR to: add three labelled snippets (Preferred: ESM, Compatibility: CJS require guard, Troubleshooting: Jest/ts-jest notes), an FAQ blurb about the `.default` symptom, and a debug script in sample-app that logs resolution method. Will tag the CI job `ci/sample-app/import-matrix` in the PR.

docs-bot: reminder: link PR to `/docs/sdk/js/imports.md` and `/sample-app/README.md` and include the CI job tag in a code comment.

maria_onboard: awesome, thanks. If anyone sees a customer repro, drop logs here and I'll include them in the FAQ. :sparkles:
